A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CORALZ project has provided us with the first complete sample of compact radio sources in nearby galaxies.
the sources in CORALZ are a low-luminosity extension of the GPS/CSS population.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the CORALZ objects are the low-luminosity counterparts of the more famous GPS and CSS objects.

the radio luminosity of the CORAL Z sources is too low to allow the sources to expand faster than 0.2c, which is the maximum expansion speed predicted by the analytical models for the evolution of radio sources.

the CORALZ radio sources are a unique sample to study the early phases in the evolution of radio sources, and that VLBI observations are essential to obtain reliable morphologies and linear sizes for these sources, as well as to determine their expansion velocities and spectral turnovers.
